<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par159 />its origin is obscure. Cf. the exhaustive discussion of Delitzsch and Wetzstein on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=36}}, where this {{GHGheb|text=אבי}} appears to be used as a desiderative particle.—Sometimes when one case has been already discussed, another of the same character is added by means of {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}} or, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ נוֹדַע וג׳|translate=or}} (another possible case) ''it is known that'', &c., i.e. ''but if it be known'', &c., LXX ἐὰν δέ, Vulg. ''sin autem''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=23}}, 28, 5:1, 25:49, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=13}}; with a following imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=17}}f.—On the hypothetical use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} (which is interchangeable with {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} in other senses also) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=22}} (in verses 3 and 27 {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=27}} (verse 28 {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=21}}, see the Lexicon.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|dd}}
2. The conditional sentence is frequently found in an abridged form, where the suppressed clauses can be easily supplied from the context; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=49|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם־לֹא|translate=and if not}}, i.e. ''and if thou wilt not give it to me, then I take'' it (perfect according to {{GHGpar|106|n}}) ''by force''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=9}}. The use of {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵשׁ}} alone in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=13}} is peculiar, as also {{GHGheb|text=וָיֵשׁ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=15}} (where read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּא֫מֶר יֵהוּא וָיֵשׁ}}) in the sense of ''if it be so''.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=וָלֹא}} alone appears to be used in the sense of ''if really ... not'', in each case with a following jussive equivalent to ''may there at least'', &c. (cf. {{GHGpar|143|d}}); but perhaps with Matthes, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1903, p. 122 ff., following Kuipers, we should read {{GHGheb|text=וְלוּ|translate=would that!}}—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=13}} the condition must be supplied from the preceding clause to complete the sentence introduced by {{GHGheb|text=כִּי עַתָּה}}, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=28}} by {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}}, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=19}} by {{GHGheb|text=אָז}}.—The apodosis also appears sometimes in an abridged form (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=2}}) or is entirely suppressed, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (see y above), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=5}}, where properly {{GHGheb|text=הַגֵּד}} must be supplied with {{GHGheb|text=כִּי תֵדָ֑ע}} as in verses 4 and 18; cf. {{GHGpar|167|a}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=4}}, instead of the apodosis ''I exclaim'' which we should expect, the exclamation itself follows.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|ee}}
3. The absolute certainty with which a result is to be expected is frequently emphasized by the insertion of {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אָזָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=15}}; or {{GHGheb|text=כִּי עַתָּה|translate=now verily}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=30}} after {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=10|hidebook=1}} after {{GHGheb|text=לוּלֵי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=6}} after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}. On this ''corroborative'' {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} cf. such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=20}}, &c., and {{GHGpar|148|d}}. On {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} after an oath cf. 163 d.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|ff}}
4. Sometimes the force of a hypothetical particle extends beyond the apodosis to a second conditional clause, as in the case of {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|159|gg}}
5. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=20}} a negative statement takes the place of a condition with a negative consequence, ''for a man doth not see me and live'', instead of ''for if a man sees me, he does not live''; cf. the similar passages, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=1}}, 4 ''thou shalt not see ... and hide thyself, instead of if thou seest ... thou shalt not hide thyself''.<section end=par159 />

<section begin=par160 />{{GHGpar-heading|160|Concessive Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|160|a}}
Besides the use of the imperative in the sense of a concession, meant either seriously ({{GHGpar|110|a}}) or mockingly ({{GHGpar|110|f}}), and of concessive circumstantial clauses ({{GHGpar|141|e}}, {{GHGpar|142|d}}, and {{GHGpar|156|f}}), concessive clauses may be introduced—

(''a'') By a simple {{GHGheb|text=אִם|translate=if}}: thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}} with perfect, ''if'' (=''though'') ''I had been in the right''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=18}} and 10:22 with imperfect in reference to a contingent event.

{{GHGmargin-letter|160|b}}
(''b'') By {{GHGheb|text=גַּם כִּי|translate=yea though}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}} with imperfect; for which we find simply {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=15}} with imperfect, ''yea, though these may forget, yet'' ...; on the other hand, with perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=1}}; finally {{GHGheb|text=כִּי גַם|translate=even if, though}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=14}}.
<section end=par160 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
